doc.title: Kidd Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006

title: Collecting and losing instruments in the flood
summary: Jordan's horns, bass clarinets and Super 20 saxophones, many lost to the flood.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: I had a lot of horns and I was a collector. I’ve been collecting horns since I had the C melody that I started on. I had that. So I had about three or four C melodies, I had all kinds of altos, I bought a straight alto. I was probably one of the first people in the United States, not from the twenties, they made one from the twenties, I sold that one, I got one of them. But I bought one in Amsterdam that was more in tune than that old one I had. But in fact I’ve still got a straight, but I had a couple basses, bassoon, about five or six bass clarinets. ‘Cause bass clarinets, when you play shows, I would have a bass clarinet in my car in the trunk, maybe two in the locker and one on the stands. ‘Cause you can look at them and they go out on you. And I had a friend of mine, he died too, he was an instrument repairman. And I remember many nights going, getting ready to walk on the stand and the bass clarinet was out. I said, “Harris, get my bass clarinet man.” “Man, we don’t have time.” I’d send somebody to the locker. Go to the locker and get one. If that didn’t work, get the other one, there’s another one in there. ‘Cause you know some of them conductors are very picky about them bass clarinet parts and so forth and so on. So I had all kinds of instruments, good quality instruments, and I lost my contrabass that I played on this session that you played from. So I had a lot of instruments and all the saxes, and my wife would look at me — do you know three days I bought a saxophone on a Tuesday, a King Super 20. I went in a pawn shop and saw it, and my wife was over shopping somewhere else. And the man told me what he wanted for it and I told my wife I said, “look I need two hundred dollars.” She said, “if you need two hundred dollars it must be a saxophone somewhere.” I bought the saxophone on a Tuesday and it had some leaks in it, and I gave it to one of my students, my repairman lived about twenty miles in a community we call Slidell. I said, “bring this to the man and get the leaks out of it ‘till it’s not leaking and bring it back to school Monday.” It was in his car, it went down in his car. But he told me that he thinks the man can fix it. I only played on it with the leaks. And I had another Super 20 that I lost, it was in the attic. And one of my good students, his horns went down. And I had given that to him about maybe a month before that, he had some kind of confusion with his family so I said here take this Super 20, and his horn went down at his family’s house so he’s still got my old Super 20. And now he asked me, he said, “man why don’t you sell it to me?” And off the cuff it’s his but I just want to
make him think. I said, “look I may walk down on a gig one night and just say, ‘give it to me.’” I will just get mad and keep it.
Keep him on edge a little bit.
Yeah, keep him on edge. MR Oh, that’s a great story. So did you — you had to evacuate?
